messages:
Evan Brooks: Pushed a lightweight design for a 'Threshold Tuning Assistant' inside the alert rule editor. The idea: show suggested thresholds based on historical traffic + a preview of how many alerts would've fired in the last 7 days.
Clara Wu: Love it. Does the preview run locally in the browser or call a service? Need to know for permission/latency implications.
Noah Patel: Backend will run a dry-run job against a cached 7-day rollup endpoint, returns an anonymized sample. Latency ~200-400ms. We'll need a small spinner.
Sam Rivera: Accessibility note: the preview summary is a data-dense widget. When results load, announce via aria-live: "Threshold preview: 12 matches in last 7 days; estimated noise 8%". Also add a 'Details' link that opens a focus-trapped modal.
Jules Martin: Copy thoughts: the header currently reads "Suggested thresholds". Suggest: "Recommended thresholds (preview)" to set expectation that it's advisory. Also microcopy under the preview: "Based on recent traffic and error rates. Use as a starting point."
Evan Brooks: Good. UX question: when recommending a threshold, do we offer multiple options (conservative / balanced / aggressive) with estimated alert counts?
Clara Wu: Yes — three presets with small chips: Conservative (low false positives), Balanced, Aggressive (low MTTD). Each chip shows a small stat: "~3 alerts/week". Clicking a chip populates the threshold fields.
Noah Patel: We should show the exact historical hit examples for the chosen preset in a short list (time + metric value) so users can eyeball edge cases. Limit to 5 samples.
Sam Rivera: For keyboard users, ensure the presets are reachable and the samples list is keyboard-navigable. Each sample should have an explicit button 'View event' that opens the full event in the audit log (new tab). Announce when 'View event' opens.
Jules Martin: Tone/voice: avoid technical jargon in the main pane. Replace 'false positives' with 'unnecessary alerts' in the main UX; keep technical terms in advanced help.
Evan Brooks: Also thinking about a 'What if' slider: let users simulate changing the threshold and see a live update of expected weekly alerts. Slider steps should be meaningful (e.g., 0.1% increments for low-rate metrics).
Clara Wu: Visualization: small sparkline + histogram + a vertical marker for the threshold. For color, use blue for values and orange for threshold line; include a pattern fill for high-intensity bars for a11y.
Noah Patel: Backend note: we can compute histogram buckets and approximate counts. We should also expose a "confidence" number derived from sample size. Show tooltip: "Confidence: medium (based on 3k samples)".
Sam Rivera: Make sure confidence tooltip is accessible. Avoid color-only confidence cues; include words and aria-labels.
Jules Martin: Copy change: change CTA from "Apply" to "Apply recommended threshold" and secondary "Preview only" so users can opt to only preview without saving.
Evan Brooks: Org-level concerns: if an org has a locked maximum severity (e.g., you can't silence P0s), then the assistant should dim options that violate org policy and show an explanation: "Disabled by org guardrails" with a link to request exceptions.
Clara Wu: For that link, show a lightweight modal to request exception with prefilled context (rule name, selected preset, why). Include an estimated SLA impact note.
Noah Patel: Logging: any applied recommended threshold should create a structured audit entry with the preset used and the preview stats. Helps postmortem.
Sam Rivera: One more a11y nit: when the slider updates the preview counts, use a polite aria-live region that reads "Preview updated: 5 alerts/week". Debounce to avoid chatter.
Jules Martin: Final microcopy tweak: in the sample list, label the metric value with units and localized number formatting (e.g., 1,234 vs 1.234). We'll surface localized examples in expanded view.
design-bot: Reminder 10am PT critique on Tuesday  add mocks + accessibility spec to the figma by EOD Monday.
Evan Brooks: Thanks all 44d I'll push updated mock with three presets, slider, sparkline, sample list, confidence tooltip, and audit hooks to the drive: https://drive.redwood/design/threshold-tuning-assistant-iter1
Clara Wu: Will iterate on pattern fills and focus states.
Noah Patel: I'll wire the preview API; will stub the sample responses for the critique.
Sam Rivera: I'll draft the aria strings and live region patterns.
Jules Martin: I'll produce final microcopy for localization. Closing thread, drop comments on the figma if you see anything.
